title: BantooBooks Tutorial
description: Formal schema for a single BantooBooks tutorial content file. Each tutorial markdown file (NNN-slug.md) has YAML frontmatter that MUST validate against this schema. See tutorials/README.md for the human-readable explanation of every field and tutorials/TEMPLATE.md for a blank starting point.

tutorial_id.description: Stable short id in kebab-case. MUST match the filename minus the leading 'NNN-' number prefix and the '.md' extension. Never change this once published — video tools and the help center will link to it.

title.description: Human-readable tutorial title, shown as the H1 / help-center article title.

feature_area.description: The product area this tutorial belongs to. Keep this list small and consistent so tutorials can be grouped/filtered later.

audience.description: Who this tutorial is written for, in plain terms (e.g. 'New BantooBooks users', 'Shop owner / cashier', 'Bookkeeper'). Used to calibrate jargon level in the voiceover and help-center article.

goal.description: One sentence describing exactly what the user accomplishes by the end of the tutorial. Should be usable as a video description opener.

prerequisites.description: Things that must already be true / set up before this tutorial can be followed (e.g. an existing bank/cash account, an existing customer, an existing inventory item).

demo_company.description: Which permanent demo organization to record this tutorial in. Use the canonical BantooBooks demo org unless a tutorial specifically needs a different seeded dataset.

test_data.description: The exact, realistic values to type or select while recording — names, amounts, dates. Must be consistent with the demo org's actual seeded data style (Cameroonian XAF FMCG distributor, real consumer brand names used only as representative catalog items, French/English mixed place names). Keys are free-form (whatever fields this tutorial's form has); values are strings so they can be typed verbatim on screen.

step_by_step_actions.description: Numbered, precise actions using REAL button/field labels exactly as they appear in the BantooBooks UI (not paraphrased). Each item is one discrete action a presenter/recorder performs.

action.description: What to click/type/select, quoting the exact UI label, e.g. 'Click the "+ Add customer" pill on the dashboard.'

screen_to_show.description: For each step, which page/panel is on screen — written for a video editor who has never used the app.

voiceover_script.description: Simple, friendly, plain-language narration for African SME users, roughly mapped 1:1 to step_by_step_actions. Avoid accounting jargon; explain WHY a step matters where useful. This script assumes the viewer CAN see the screen (unlike synthesia_script).

on_screen_highlights.description: What to visually emphasize, circle, or zoom in on at each step, for a video editor adding call-outs in Guidde or a similar tool.

expected_result.description: What the user should see/verify at the end, in concrete, checkable terms (e.g. 'The customer count on the Customers page increases by 1 and the new name appears in the list.').

youtube_description.description: 2-4 sentences plus a short bullet list (as markdown '- ' lines within the string, or use youtube_description_bullets) written for discoverability (search terms an SME owner would type).

help_center_article.description: A short, self-contained written how-to (a few paragraphs) that could stand alone as a help doc, independent of any video.

guidde_recording_notes.description: Practical notes for whoever records this in Guidde: browser zoom level, things to blur/avoid showing (real customer data, API keys, other orgs in the switcher, etc.), pacing tips, click-precision notes.

synthesia_script.description: A separate, tightly-timed narrator script for an AI avatar tool. Short sentences, natural pauses marked with '...' or line breaks, target ~60-90 seconds spoken (roughly 150-220 words). Must stand alone with NO visual-only references ('as you can see', 'click here', 'this button') since the Synthesia viewer may not be shown the matching screen recording.
